title: Practical LLM Field Notes: pieces to try + conference sparks
content:
Context: quick working notes after ML Systems meetup + two papers skimmed. Goal is a lightweight list of ideas to prototype in the next sprint (Dedicated + Private tests), and a short runnable mental model of tradeoffs we care about (latency SLO, p99 tail, token-cost).

High-level takeaways (one-liners):
- Small changes to cache sharding and eviction policy produced disproportionate p99 wins in talk demos — worth trying a few pragmatic versions in our test harness.
- Adaptive micro-batching that uses a live estimate of token-latency per-model (>single scalar) looks promising to reduce cost without slamming SLOs.
- Quant-stability: some 4-bit recipes give nice throughput gains but subtle generation drift on longer contexts; need short eval suites that detect exact-token shifts, not just semantic parity.

Papers / posts skimmed (notes):
1) "Grouped-KV Cache Sharding for Low-Tail Latency" (arXiv 2026)
   - Core idea: shard KV store by recent-token affinity instead of only by request source. Lightweight lookup to pick the best shard(s) for prefetch.
   - Why it matters: reduces cross-GPU kv fetch events for some long-tail flows. In demo, p99 improved >> median.
   - Quick questions: how much extra memory overhead for duplicate entries across shards? Can we piggyback on our current LRU+segmented-eviction?
   - How to try: implement a toy sharder in local bench — simulate 16 simulated clients with synthetic context reuse curves. Compare naive global cache vs grouping by recent n-gram fingerprints.

2) "Latency-Aware Microbatching with Per-Request Deadlines" (conference workshop)
   - Idea: attach soft deadline metadata to each request, scheduler forms batches that maximize GPU utilization while keeping deadlines for tight requests.
   - Practical angle: we already have per-customer route latency goals; extend scheduler to accept per-request deadline and return partial results when deadlines near.
   - Danger: increased scheduler complexity and fairness issues. Need deterministic fallback (if deadline not achievable, route to lighter model).

3) "Quant drift and chain-of-thought fidelity under 3/4-bit" (blog + replications)
   - Observation: hallucination rates not huge but chain-of-thought coherence degrades after 512 tokens in some configs.
   - Takeaway: include targeted chain-of-thought prompts in our compact eval sets; track token-level perplexity and BLEU-ish overlap for short windows to catch drift early.

Notes from the meetup (practical actions):
- Demo by S. Choi showing prefix-hint caching: store short compressed snippets of KV for common phrase prefixes and rehydrate quickly. Good for assistant workflows with repeated phrases. Action: prototype a prefix-index for top-10k n-grams from logs.
- Panel on "observable SLOs": people favored synthetic golden-prompts + live shadowing. For us, add a nightly run of 50 golden prompts per-catalog-model and diff logits for early-warning.

Concrete experiments to land in next sprint (priority ordered):
1) KV grouping prototype (low-effort):
   - implement a fingerprint function (sha1 of last 16 tokens -> bucket) in bench harness.
   - simulate 10k requests with context reuse distribution sampled from production logs (use redwood-sim dataset).
   - metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, extra memory duplication fraction, cold-start miss-rate.

2) Deadline-aware microbatch scheduler (medium):
   - extend local scheduler to accept per-request deadline (ms).
   - implement simple greedy batch assembly: earliest deadline first, but allow opportunistic fill until next-deadline slack threshold.
   - fallback policy: if deadline cannot be met, drop into lightweight-model route (e.g., 1/2 quant variant).

3) 4-bit quant drift quick-eval (quick-turn):
   - add chain-of-thought set of 200 prompts (from prior evals) and compute token-by-token KL / edit-distance to FP16 run.
   - flag delta-thresholds.

Small code sketch (pseudocode to implement in bench harness):
- fingerprint = last16tokens.hash() % 256
- assign_to_shard = hash(user_id) ^ fingerprint
- if shard_cache[assign_to_shard].has(prefix): prefetch(shard_cache[assign_to_shard].get(prefix))

Open questions / unknowns:
- How will duplication across shards affect our Dedicated capacity billing model? If duplication increases memory beyond a GPU's soft limit, we need an eviction-aware placement policy.
- Can deadline-based batching be done without adding jitter that hurts median latency? Need microbench measurement across arrival patterns.
- For quant drift: is the drift model additive (worse with each quantization stage) or input-distribution dependent? Need controlled experiments with similar prompts but varying topic shifts.

References quick-list:
- arXiv:2601.01234 (grouped-KV)
- internal PR: github.com/redwood-inference/kv-shard-prototypes#47 (early experiments)
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime:kv-eviction-discuss (link pinned)

Personal next steps (this week):
- Draft bench harness changes for KV grouping and share with Samir by Wed.
- Put together small chain-of-thought probe set and run FP16 vs 4-bit on 5 models to get baseline numbers. Expect ~3h to run.
- Quick doc for SRE: note memory-dup risk and ask for guidance on capacity test cluster window.

Notes-to-self (loose):
- Keep experiments small and measurable. Each change should have one primary metric.
- Record seed and prompt sampling method for reproducibility.
- If promising, fold into Redwood Optimize as "kv-affinity suggestion" for customers who care about tail latency.

End of page — rough, half-baked, actionable. Will refine after prototype numbers.
